<!-- pr-reviewer: 0aef90a5dad59d5d397b830b26684691597044b8 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (one small blocker: clippy).

Thank you @tbrasselle - this is a well-structured contribution. Red pins first, a role API that returns the existing `Alignment`, and it reuses the undoable `SetWcs` rather than adding a command.

**What looks good**
- Everything Is a Command holds: Apply queues the existing `CommandKind::SetWcs` (`wcs_pick_row.rs`); the draft is ephemeral UI state, and no world writes happen outside commands.
- Refusals come back by name from `align_roles` and the UI shows the app's own words on the disabled Apply, so there is one source for the "why".
- `crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs` has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. Degenerate wall fits and missing datums return `Err`.
- Layering is respected (ui calls `pick::align_roles`; no component declared outside `schema.rs`). Provenance lines are present on the new modules. The decision file `docs/decisions/701-wcs-from-features.md` exists. No dependency, `build.rs`, script or `.github` changes. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #701`, and commit subjects are conventional.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit in the PR.

**Local results (PR head merged with upstream/main `4827fde6`; the merge was a no-op, the branch is already on current main and mergeable)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` | 6 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 103 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (from `crates/ui`) | 430 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` | FAILED, 5 errors, all in `roles.rs` |

```
error: this `if` statement can be collapsed          crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:123:13
error: the loop variable `i` is used to index `v`    crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:435:14
error: the loop variable `k` is only used to index `a`  crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:452:22
error: the loop variable `k` is only used to index `a`  crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:457:22
error: the loop variable `k` is only used to index `v`  crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:462:22
```
I did not build the unrelated `lathe_thread_travel` test (known #686), only the touched suites.

**Requested before merge**
1. Clear the five clippy lints above (`roles.rs:123` collapse the nested `if let`/`if`; `:435`, `:452`, `:457`, `:462` use iterators, or an `#[allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]` with a one-line reason on the small 3x3 Jacobi). The gate runs clippy with `-D warnings`.
2. `crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs` is 477 lines, over the ~400-line law as a new file. Please split along the seam you already have, e.g. move the wall fit (`fit_wall`, `perp_basis`, `jacobi_sym3`, roughly lines 300-477) into `pick/wall_fit.rs`.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Overlap with #692, for the maintainer: PR #705 (feature graph and pick API) and draft PR #709 (rewires every UI picker through one pick rule) both touch `interact.rs`, `vertex_pick.rs` and `crates/app/src/pick.rs`, as this PR does. #706 adds `wcs_pick::collecting` branches in `interact.rs` `pick_face`/`pick_edge` and its own `datum_for`/`wall_datum` resolution from `GeoSel`, which #705/#709 will probably replace with the graph's feature types. Expect textual conflicts in `interact.rs` and `pick.rs` once either lands, and the `GeoSel`-based datum code may later want to read from the new feature graph. This is a duplication question for the maintainer, not a defect here.
- `wcs_pick.rs:118,131,142` use `expect` in tests only, which is fine.
- `interact.rs` (1788 lines) and `state.rs` (4065) were already over the 400-line law; this PR adds a little to them, which is not blocking.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 5237db0611215724af0f73f9fa29bbc9d3acbb47 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (one correctness blocker in the frame maths; the earlier clippy and file-size blockers are fixed).

Thank you @tbrasselle - the review fixes landed cleanly, and this is a tidy contribution.

**Earlier blockers**
- Five clippy lints in `roles.rs`: fixed, clippy is clean at this head.
- `roles.rs` over 400 lines: fixed, the wall fit now lives in `pick/wall_fit.rs` (roles 283, wall_fit 205).
- The branch is already merged with current main (it contains `upstream/main`; trial merge was a no-op), so the stale `conflicts` label is dropped.

**What looks good**
- Everything Is a Command holds: Apply queues the existing `CommandKind::SetWcs` -> `SetWcsOrigin` (undoable, undo restores the previous frame; the kittest pins round-trip it). The draft is ephemeral view state; non-finite angles are refused in the handler.
- Picks are read through `setup_align::view_pose`, the same frame #326/#738/#746 use for setup alignment, so the result composes with an aligned setup instead of fighting it. It reuses `align`'s `straight_edge`/`vertex`/`outward_normal` and `face_origin` rather than duplicating them, and the #709 pick wire (`feature_click`) carries the new draft with a one-line hook.
- Refusals are by name: too few picks, duplicate role, fewer than two axes, parallel axes (5 degree tilt rule), zero-length/curved/closed edge, flat or non-round wall, stale feature, non-finite result. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests (the three in `wcs_pick.rs` are test-only).
- Layering is respected, no new components, provenance lines on all new modules, all files under 400 lines, decision file present, no snapshot PNG, process-file, dependency, `build.rs` or `.github` changes. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #701`.

**Local results (merged with main)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` | 6 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 107 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (from `crates/ui`) | 461 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
1. `crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs:~110` (`let a = d1.dir.ok_or_else(...)`): when the FIRST axis pick is a straight edge, `datum_for` returns the raw `b - a` walk as `dir` (roles.rs ~line 218), and `a` is used unnormalised as the frame axis. The second axis is normalised by `square_to`, but the first and the derived third (`cross(a, x)`) carry the edge's length, so `Alignment.x/y/z` are not orthonormal and `quat_from_axes` (Shepperd on a scaled matrix) returns a wrong rotation, silently. Reproduced locally on a 20x20x10 block pitched 25 degrees about X: Z = the block's vertical 10 mm edge, X = its +X side face gives `y = [0, 9.06, 4.23]`, `z = [0, -4.23, 9.06]` and roll 45.56 degrees, where the same frame from the top face gives `y`, `z` unit and roll 25 degrees. For an axis-aligned part it happens to look right (identity), which is why the pins miss it. Fix: normalise `a` (refuse non-finite or zero length by name) right after reading it, and add a pin with an edge as Z (or X) on a tilted part asserting orthonormal axes and the expected euler angles. This is the Prime Directive case: a wrong WCS rotation posts shifted toolpaths with no diagnostic.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- MCP: no new command is added (it reuses `SetWcs`), so the "commands ship with an MCP tool" rule is not triggered; the MCP `set_wcs` takes an absolute origin/quaternion only. A follow-up `MCP: set WCS from feature picks` issue (`area:mcp`, P1, `source:agent`) would keep the agent surface level with the GUI - please name one in the body if you file it.
- The role row takes faces, edges, vertices and walls but not the arc/circle centres from #705/#692 (`PickKinds.centres: false` in `feature_click.rs`), so a hole-rim centre cannot be the Origin pick yet. A natural follow-up now that `feature_arc` has landed.
- `interact.rs` and `state.rs` were already over the 400-line law; this PR adds only a few lines to `state.rs`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: e36c9d08d6080ddbb21ea9f3140ee1125aebb0f1 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge** (one blocker: the row can move a different setup's WCS than the one it is drawn for. The earlier frame-maths blocker is fixed.)

Thank you @tbrasselle - the normalisation fix is exactly right and its pin is a good one.

**Earlier blockers**
- First-axis edge read unnormalised (`roles.rs`): fixed in `816ed931`. `a` is normalised right after reading, a zero or non-finite length is refused by name, and `wcs_roles::an_edge_as_the_first_axis_reads_unit_on_a_part_tipped_off_the_table` pins unit and square axes, the 25 degree roll and the origin on the tipped block. Passes here.
- Clippy and the 400-line split (round 1): still fixed.

**What looks good**
- Frame law per combination: the first axis reads exactly (unit), the second is projected square to it with the 5 degree lean rule, the third is the right-handed cross. All six (first, second) role orders build a right-handed orthonormal frame. Degenerate input is refused by name: too few picks, a role set twice, fewer than two axes, a vertex as an axis, an edge as the origin, parallel axes, a zero-length edge, a flat or non-round wall, a stale feature, a non-finite result. No NaN reaches `SetWcs`, and the state handler refuses non-finite angles again.
- One source of truth: nothing here derives a WCS or a work offset (G54-G59). Apply queues the existing undoable `SetWcs` -> `SetWcsOrigin`, which writes the setup's WCS entity and keeps the previous location for undo. The kittest pin round-trips undo and redo. No new command, so the MCP rule is not triggered.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. All new files are under 400 lines. Layering is ui -> app. No new components. Provenance lines are on every new module. The decision file is present. No goldens, snapshot PNGs, process files, dependencies, `build.rs` or `.github` are touched. UI text is plain English.

**Local results (PR head merged with `origin/main` `9630c86e`, which includes #908; the merge is clean)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` | 7 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 108 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 533 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
1. **Apply on another setup's row moves the ACTIVE setup's WCS.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_pick_row.rs:92` queues `CommandKind::SetWcs`, and `SetWcsOrigin::new` (`crates/app/src/commands/set_wcs.rs:38`) always places `setup::active`'s WCS. But the row is drawn on every setup's settings page (`setup_pages.rs:170`, which also shows inactive setups - that is why the page has the "Active setup" radio), and the draft records `setup`. So with Setup1 active, using the row on Setup2's page silently moves Setup1's work zero, and the status line reads "WCS (G54) origin set". Every program posted from Setup1 then shifts. The sibling rows do not have this problem: they send their setup by name (`LayPartOnPlane { setup, .. }`, `setup_plane_pick.rs:118`).
   Reproduction (local test, not pushed): `with_part()`, then `CreateSetup` (Setup2) and `ActivateSetup(Setup1)`. Draw `wcs_pick_row::row(ui, st, "Setup2")`, pick top face as Z, edge (0,0,10)-(20,0,10) as X and corner (20,20,10) as Origin, then click Apply:
   ```
   setups ["Setup1", "Setup2"] active Some("Setup1")
   Setup1 None -> Some([20.0, 20.0, 10.0])
   Setup2 None -> None
   status WCS (G54) origin set
   ```
   Fix: make Apply place the row's own setup. Either (a) grey Apply out unless `setup == setup::active(world)`, saying why on the disabled button ("Make <setup> the active setup to set its WCS from features"); or (b) give the command a setup target. Note that `align_roles` reads picks through `view_pose`, which is the active setup's frame. So (b) would also have to read the picks in that setup's frame, and (a) is the smaller change. Please add a kittest pin with two setups, the row on the inactive one, which asserts that the active setup's WCS is unchanged.

**Notes (non-blocking)**
- MCP: as round 2 noted, the MCP `set_wcs` takes only an absolute origin and quaternion. A follow-up `MCP: set WCS from feature picks` issue (`area:mcp`, P1) would keep the agent surface level with the GUI. Please name it in the body if you file it.
- A wall picked as an axis takes its sign from the +Z / +Y / +X hemisphere rule (`wall_fit.rs`), not from the origin pick as an edge does. That is deterministic, but a horizontal bore picked as X can come out pointing the "wrong" way along the bore. Siding a wall axis by the origin pick (like edges) would match what a user expects.
- Without an Origin pick the origin falls on the second axis pick's anchor (an edge's start, a face's centroid, a wall's centre), projected onto the first pick's plane when that pick is a face. The PR body says "without one the origin stays the model's own", which no longer matches the code. Please update the body, or the decision file.
- `e36c9d08` (the refusal-ghost `diag_warn!`) is the same change as #908, which is now on main. The merge is clean, so it simply folds in.
- The test counts in the body's "Tested" section are from an earlier head (103 app lib, 430 ui lib).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d2663a3f8d954649a051d8bfa7268b03938def06 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thank you @tbrasselle - the round-3 blocker is fixed the way the review suggested, and it has a good pin.

**Earlier blocker (Apply on another setup's row moved the ACTIVE setup's WCS)**
- Fixed in `9645bee6` (option a). `wcs_pick_row.rs` computes `active = setup::active(world) == Some(row's setup)`; Apply is enabled only when `check.is_ok() && active`, and the disabled button/tooltip reads "Make <setup> the active setup to set its WCS from features". Nothing is queued from an inactive row.
- Pinned by `wcs_pick_tests::the_row_on_an_inactive_setup_cannot_move_another_setups_work_zero` (two setups, row on the inactive one, whole frame picked: Apply stays grey, the message shows, the active setup's WCS is unchanged; once Setup2 is made active the same frame moves Setup2's own WCS and Setup1's stays put). It passes here.
- Earlier rounds (clippy, 400-line split, first-axis normalisation) remain fixed.

**What looks good**
- Everything Is a Command: Apply queues the existing undoable `SetWcs` -> `SetWcsOrigin`; the draft is ephemeral UI state. No new command, so no MCP tool owed here (the follow-up is filed as #937).
- Refusals are by name from `align_roles`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. Layering ui -> app, no new components, provenance lines on new modules, decision file present. New/edited modules are under 400 lines (`state.rs` was already far over; the PR adds a field and one hook line).
- No snapshot PNGs, process files, `CHANGELOG.md`, dependency, `build.rs`, script or `.github` changes. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #701`; commit subjects are conventional.

**Local results (PR head merged with upstream/main `f490458a`; already up to date, no conflicts)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` | 7 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 110 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 538 passed, 5 ignored with `--test-threads=1` (a parallel run showed the known `law_tests`/`path_lines` race reds, unrelated; all green serially) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- A wall picked as an axis takes its sign from the hemisphere rule rather than from the origin pick; deterministic, and already listed under Follow-ups.
- MCP parity for feature picks is tracked in #937.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4842474ee1ffc21db4df1325013e0bbf4949f304 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thank you @tbrasselle - the round-5 blocker (the Z+Y pair building a frame turned 120 degrees) is fixed exactly as asked, in `1d679350`.

**Round-5 blocker, verified**
- `crates/app/src/pick/roles.rs` (Z, Y) arm now reads `let y = square_to(g2, d2.dir, a, tilt)?; (cross(y, a), y, a)`: Z = the Z pick, Y = the Y pick projected square to it, X = Y x Z. Right-handed and orthonormal by construction; the derived axis is never the projected one.
- The three arms left are exactly the priority-ordered pairs (`AXIS_PRIORITY` = Z, X, Y gives Z+X, Z+Y, X+Y). The unreachable (X,Z), (Y,Z), (Y,X) arms are gone; anything else falls to the named refusal "two different axes set the frame - re-pick one of them".
- Pins: `a_z_face_a_y_edge_and_a_corner_build_the_upright_frame` (the reviewer's repro: x (1,0,0), y (0,1,0), z (0,0,1), pos on the corner, rpy 0) and `every_reachable_pair_puts_each_pick_on_its_own_axis` (all three pairs on a block tipped 25 degrees: each pick's role axis equals its own pick direction to 1e-9, and x = y x z). Degenerate-role refusals stay pinned by `every_degenerate_role_set_is_refused_by_name`.
- Wording matches the two-axes law: refusal is now "set the WCS from two axes, plus an optional origin" (roles.rs:82) and the Pick hover reads "Two axes place the WCS, plus an optional origin" (wcs_pick_row.rs:39); the UI test and the wcs_roles refusal asserts were updated to match.
- The change is confined to roles.rs, two test files and one hover string; no process, snapshot, dependency, build.rs, script or CHANGELOG changes.

**Local results (PR head merged with upstream/main `62a2c93a`, clean merge)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` | 9 passed |
| `wcs_align`, `wcs_view_pose`, `one_wcs`, `rotated_wcs`, `setup_defines_wcs`, `setup_wcs` | 5, 3, 8, 9, 4, 7 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` (incl. pick) | 146 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --test-threads=1` (CWD `crates/ui`; includes `wcs_pick` and structural) | 601 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The earlier non-blocking notes still stand: `wall_datum` falls back to an identity pose / silently drops missing facets and would be better refused by name; the wall axis sign rule; the body's origin wording.
- There is no test named `circle_centre` in this tree, so nothing by that name was run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
